documents.abstract: The relevance of the study. The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and neural interfaces underscores the need for a socio-philosophical analysis of transhumanism as a philosophical movement that advocates the possibility and desirability of technologically enhancing human nature. As digital society takes shape, transhumanist ideas are moving beyond academic discourse to become a driving force behind real-world social transformations, raising fundamentally new questions about the nature of human agency, the boundaries between the natural and the artificial, and the future social order. This article aims to examine the socio-philosophical dimensions of transhumanism in the age of artificial intelligence through an analysis of the movement’s key conceptual foundations, its interconnection with the processes of digitalisation, and a critical reflection on the associated risks and prospects. The study’s methodological framework is based on its stated aim and research objectives and adopts an interdisciplinary approach drawing on social philosophy, technology ethics, the social sciences, and media studies. The study employs comparative- historical analysis, the phenomenological method, critical discourse analysis, and a systems approach to investigating the social consequences of technological development. Research findings. The intellectual origins of transhumanism have been traced, from FM-2030’s futurist manifestos to contemporary concepts of the technological singularity and superintelligence. The analysis shows that digital society creates a distinct socio-technical environment in which transhumanist transformations assume concrete forms and give rise to new social tensions. Three key tensions within the transhumanist project have been identified: between individual freedom of self-improvement and its systemic social consequences; between techno-optimistic predictions and the real risks of humanity losing control over powerful technological systems; and between the pursuit of boundless self-improvement and the threat posed by the erosion of essential human qualities as the foundation of moral and legal equality. It is emphasised that a socio-philosophical understanding of transhumanism requires moving beyond the binary opposition between techno-optimism and technophobia in favour of a balanced, critical, and humanistically oriented approach that combines recognition of the genuine possibilities of technological progress with responsible consideration of its limits and risks.

documents.abstract: Introduction Trust in artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes how young people evaluate information and public issues, yet evidence from Arab contexts remains limited. This study examined the socio-technical correlates of trust in AI and its association with AI-assisted social and civic decision-making among digitally engaged youth in Egypt, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 1,023 respondents aged 18–35 recruited through purposive, non-probability sampling. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), structural equation modeling (SEM), multi-group CFA, and competing full- versus partial-mediation models evaluated measurement and structural relationships. Results The partially mediated model fit significantly better than the fully mediated model, Δχ2(5) = 55.66, p < 0.001. Institutional confidence (β = 0.303), AI literacy (β = 0.281), perceived usefulness (β = 0.242), and social influence (β = 0.107) were positively associated with trust in AI, and perceived risk was negatively associated (β = −0.106; all p < 0.001). Trust was positively associated with AI-assisted decision-making (β = 0.412, p < 0.001). Significant indirect associations through trust were observed for all five antecedents, while the direct perceived-risk path to AI-assisted decision-making was nonsignificant. Multi-group CFA supported metric and practical scalar measurement invariance across the three countries. Discussion The findings support a socio-technical account of AI trust in which technological, cognitive, institutional, and social conditions jointly relate to AI-assisted decision-making, with trust functioning as a central but not exclusive pathway. Given the cross-sectional, purposive design, findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal or nationally representative effects.

documents.abstract: Cross-institutional clinical artificial intelligence is constrained by fragmented patient data, non-identically distributed (non-IID) populations, leakage from shared model updates, and limited interpretability. Federated learning (FL) preserves data locality, but ordinary FL neither makes model updates confidential nor guarantees stable optimization under heterogeneous clients. This paper proposes a defense-in-depth framework that coordinates Federated Proximal (FedProx) optimization, record-level differential privacy (DP), Cheon–Kim–Kim–Song (CKKS) approximate homomorphic encryption, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). FedProx limits local model drift; DP-SGD bounds the influence of an individual training record; and CKKS permits weighted aggregation while client updates remain encrypted. A key-separated design keeps the aggregation server from being provisioned with the secret key used to reveal individual contributions; only the aggregate is released for global-model construction. Grad-CAM and SHAP/LIME provide clinician-facing explanations, while an audit dashboard reports convergence, privacy-accounting inputs, encryption status, and systems overhead. We formalize the learning objective, privacy mechanism, encrypted aggregation, threat model, numerical approximation error, communication footprint, and an evaluation protocol spanning IID and controlled non-IID partitions. The contribution is a reproducible system-level co-design and evaluation framework rather than a new cryptographic primitive or optimization algorithm.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly entering dental education, and recent reviews report both its benefits and recurring concerns about factual inaccuracy, academic integrity, over-reliance, bias, and privacy. Existing responses are largely technical and regulatory; they specify what should be done but say little about the character of the educators and students who use AI. This critical integrative review proposes a Christian virtue framework, grounded in the doctrine of the imago Dei, to guide dental educators and students. Empirical literature on AI in dental and health-professions education was read alongside Catholic and evangelical documents on AI and Christian scholarship on education and personhood. Five virtues, identified from Christian virtue-ethics literature on AI, were mapped to the main AI issues: truthfulness (hallucinated content and academic integrity), practical wisdom (automation bias, overconfidence, and deskilling), responsibility (accountability for AI-supported decisions), justice (bias and unequal access), and love (empathy, the clinician–patient relationship, and privacy). For each virtue, implications for educators and students are outlined. The framework suggests that responsible AI use in dental education is a matter not only of policy but also of formation, and it offers Christian dental schools a basis for curricula and institutional guidance.

documents.abstract: Art and design education expects students to develop a sense of authorship over original work, but generative AI (GenAI) complicates how students understand and claim that authorship. This study examined whether these experiences differ across creative fields through a mixed-methods design. The survey included 2,441 GenAI-using students from seven field categories at 33 art and design institutions in China and assessed authorship anxiety, creative agency, perceived usefulness, dependence on GenAI, and frequency of use. The quantitative analysis first examined variation across all seven categories and then compared fine art with the five applied design fields. Interview data from 22 survey participants were also examined thematically. The main findings include that (1) authorship anxiety did not differ significantly across the seven categories or between fine art and pooled design; the latter comparison met the equivalence criterion at ±d = 0.20, but not at tighter bounds; (2) clearer differences emerged in how students used GenAI. Compared with fine-art students, design students considered GenAI more useful and used it more frequently; (3) across the interviews, most students described authorship as retaining control over the creative idea while delegating parts of its execution to GenAI. Specifically, fine-art students often grounded authorship in embodied making and human imperfection, whereas design students placed greater emphasis on judgement, selection, and control. We call this pattern uneven automation: concern about authorship was broadly shared, but students in different fields responded to GenAI in different ways, potentially reflecting the varying labour-market pressures surrounding their disciplines.

BACKGROUND Short-answer questions (SAQs) effectively assess higher-order reasoning skills in medical education but face challenges in scalability due to time-intensive manual grading and concerns about interrater reliability. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) may offer a solution through automated assessment. OBJECTIVE This study evaluated the performance and consistency of LLMs—ChatGPT, Claude Sonnet 4, and Mistral Pro—compared with those of human graders for SAQ grading in hepatology and gastroenterology. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed SAQs from hepatology and gastroenterology examinations at Sorbonne University, Paris, France (2023-2025). Three human evaluators (2 hepatogastroenterologists and 1 radiologist) independently graded all responses twice, with the majority consensus score serving as the reference standard. Six LLMs were evaluated: ChatGPT (GPT-4o, GPT-4.5, GPT-4o3, and GPT-5), Claude Sonnet 4, and Mistral Pro. Each LLM graded all responses twice using standardized prompts, including questions, model answers, grading guidelines, and scoring rubrics. Agreement was assessed using quadratic weighted kappa (QWK), Cohen κ, the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and the mean absolute error (MAE) for interhuman, intrahuman, LLM-versus-human, and intramodel comparisons. RESULTS A total of 902 student responses from 12 SAQs were included and analyzed. Interhuman grader agreement was almost perfect (QWK 0.90-0.92; ICC 0.90-0.92; MAE 0.05-0.07). Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-4o3 demonstrated near-human–level performance when compared with the majority vote of human evaluators (Claude Sonnet 4: QWK 0.88-0.90; ICC 0.88-0.90; MAE 0.06-0.07 and GPT-4o3: QWK 0.82-0.89; ICC 0.82-0.89; MAE 0.07-0.09). GPT-5 showed substantial agreement (QWK 0.77-0.79). Mistral Pro and older ChatGPT versions performed poorly (QWK <0.63). Intramodel consistency was the highest for Claude Sonnet 4 (QWK 0.93), approaching the best human intrarater reliability. Agreement did not correlate with prompt design choices (number of examples or minimum word count). CONCLUSIONS Advanced LLMs, particularly Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-4o3, demonstrated near-human–level grading performance, supporting their potential use as assistive tools in SAQ grading. However, performance varied by model, and agreement alone does not ensure educational validity. Until broader multicenter validation is conducted across diverse domains, stakes, and question formats—along with safeguards for bias, privacy, and model drift—LLMs should augment rather than replace human faculty graders.

documents.abstract: PURPOSE: Contemporary neurosurgical training faces challenges due to reduced operative exposure and the limited, inconsistent feedback provided to trainees. Wearable technologies may help address these issues by offering objective data and real-time support. This scoping review systematically evaluates the evidence of wearable technology in surgical training, analysing device types, their applications, and the supporting evidence for their effectiveness. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in 10 pre-clinical and clinical databases from inception to May 2024, searching for keywords "wearable technology" AND "surgery" AND "training". The search yielded 25,806 results. After removing duplicates, papers were screened by title and abstract (n = 12,306), followed by full-text screening (n = 482). RESULTS: Forty-one studies, including 985 participants, were included in the review. Head-mounted displays were predominantly used for augmented and mixed reality applications, while smart glasses facilitated telementoring and procedure recording. Other wearables enabled biomechanical analysis and ergonomic assessments. Reported outcomes varied widely, with clinician-centred metrics, such as procedural accuracy, error rates, completion times, and satisfaction, being the most frequently assessed. Devices including HTC VIVE and HoloLens were associated with improved surgical performance. Clinicians often reported enhanced visualisation and anatomical orientation, though barriers such as learning curves, technical issues, and discomfort were noted. CONCLUSIONS: This review provides a comprehensive evaluation of wearable technologies in surgical training, highlighting their potential to improve performance metrics and support a range of educational uses for neurosurgical trainees. However, key challenges must be addressed to enable broader adoption and integration into surgical education.

documents.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) advertising, defined as advertising content created or substantially assisted by generative AI systems (AIGC), has introduced new visual features that combine algorithmically generated objects with human-like representations. Hyper-salient objects, defined by exaggerated perceptual prominence and semantic incongruity, and AI-generated virtual endorsers, represented by human-like AI-created figures, have become increasingly common in such advertisements. However, little is known about how these distinct visual cues compete for consumers’ limited attentional resources when presented together. Drawing on visual attention and scene perception perspectives, this study investigated how hyper-salient objects and AI-generated virtual endorsers influence visual attention allocation in AI-generated advertising. A 2 (hyper-salient object: present vs. absent) × 2 (AI endorser: present vs. absent) between-subjects eye-tracking experiment was conducted with 160 participants in a controlled laboratory setting using static AI-generated advertisements. Eye movements were recorded, and memory was assessed using signal detection measures (d′) from a recognition task involving target and distractor advertisements. Advertising attitude and product trust were measured using established scales. Results from linear and generalized linear mixed-effects models showed that hyper-salient objects increased early fixation probability and attracted a larger dwell time proportion, demonstrating strong attentional capture. AI-generated endorsers also attracted attention when presented alone, but their proportional attention share decreased when hyper-salient objects were simultaneously present. The effects of these visual elements on memory and product trust were conditional on their co-occurrence rather than uniform across conditions. Within the specific set of experimentally constructed stimuli and four sampled product categories, this research contributes to AIGC advertising literature by developing a visual competition perspective on how multiple AI-generated visual cues interact under limited attentional capacity, offering implications for designing effective generative AI advertisements.

Public guidance on generative AI asks students to exercise judgement while institutions and platforms define the conditions of use. This study examines how these texts distribute authority over writing, evidence and assessment. The purposively selected corpus comprises eight official webpages from three UK universities and Google and captions from three educational videos, retrieved in October 2026. Appraisal-informed critical discourse analysis examines 30 decision-focused units: passages addressing a particular choice or responsibility. Analysis also considers modality and legitimation, meaning the reasons offered to justify a practice. The main finding is boundary maintenance: texts distinguish what fluent writing, technical capability or disclosure can establish about learning, reliability and permission. University guidance and Gemini promotion both value learner participation, although they serve different purposes. Staff guidance also encourages discussion of assessment criteria. These findings suggest that teachers should explain acceptable assistance, student responsibilities and opportunities to question criteria. The small documentary corpus supports interpretation of published communications, not conclusions about classroom practice or AI effectiveness.

This paper examines why cryptocurrency exchanges remain vulnerable to cyberattacks by comparing two security incidents: Bybit in February 2025 and Binance in October 2026. Using statements from the companies involved, news reports, and data from 220 cryptocurrency exchange incidents between 2009 and 2024, the study explores common vulnerabilities, attack methods, financial impacts, and potential solutions.The findings identify recurring vulnerabilities, including wallet and key compromises, unauthorized access, human error, and third-party services. The paper also discusses emerging risks associated with quantum computing and AI agents with financial capabilities. In addition, it presents security recommendations such as improved key management, secure transaction processes, stronger employee and third-party security, and better recovery plans.The Binance incident is still under investigation; therefore, some reported figures and findings may change.

Generative AI (genAI) systems have become an integral part of scientific text-producing practice. They can conduct literature-related research, organize content and information, proofread text, and assist with writing itself. Above all, they are credited with reducing workload by taking on or taking over these routine tasks. Drawing on an internal, interdisciplinary KIT-ITAS project that deployed the genAI-supported research assistance system 'Undermind.ai', we demonstrate that the potential to reduce workload is offset by the need to reorganize basic scientific competencies in response to the changing workflow requirements of genAI-assisted knowledge work. GenAI systems produce texts that closely resemble stylistic conventions and appear both well-formed and plausible. However, the closer these texts adhere to researchers’ expectations, the more challenging it becomes to verify their content using established academic methods. This generates higher-order efforts that must be weighed against existing working standards for assessing text-based results. The constant validation and ongoing negotiation of plausibility with the system’s output, both during and beyond the writing process, places additional demands on researchers’ critical competence and judgement. Using genAI in knowledge work thus shifts the focus of familiar textual and intellectual labour practices and procedures away from independent creation and toward the verification of textual output, along with the corresponding demands on epistemic attention, responsibility, authorization, and authority.

documents.abstract: Targeted inhibitors of the RAS signaling pathway have moved from a historically undruggable target class to a growing portfolio of clinically active agents in advanced solid tumors, including pancreatic, colorectal, and non-small cell lung cancer. This article is written from the perspective of a clinical trial manager responsible for carrying a RAS pathway inhibitor program from its initial Investigational New Drug (IND) application or Clinical Trial Application (CTA) through the protocol amendments that inevitably follow as early clinical data accumulate. It reviews the mechanistic rationale for this drug class, the rationale for trial phase, setting, and population selection, best practices for first-in-human and dose-expansion protocol design, anticipated risks and pharmacovigilance monitoring strategy, statistical sample-size rationale drawn from registered trials, the detailed regulatory requirements, templates, and timelines governing both the initial IND or CTA submission and subsequent amendments under FDA, Health Canada, and EMA frameworks, a representative schedule of assessments spanning a twelve-month treatment period, and the application of artificial intelligence tools to data capture and data quality. The article closes with recommendations for regulatory affairs and clinical operations professionals managing this therapeutic category.Keywords: RAS pathway inhibitors; KRAS; protocol amendment; Investigational New Drug application; Clinical Trial Application; pharmacovigilance; sample size; regulatory artificial intelligence

Исследование основано на практическом вопросе, с которым всё чаще сталкиваются органы государственного планирования в Центральной Азии: насколько надёжны линейные модели при оценке влияния цифровизации, искусственного интеллекта и факторов устойчивого развития и достаточна ли их предсказательная способность для описания реальных социально-экономических процессов? Для ответа на данный вопрос была сформирована сбалансированная панель данных по 34 развивающимся экономикам и экономикам переходного типа за 2012–2024 гг., включая пять стран Центральной Азии: Узбекистан, Казахстан, Кыргызстан, Таджикистан и Туркменистан. В исследовании использованы открытые базы данных Всемирного банка (World Development Indicators), Международного союза электросвязи (ICT Development Index), Всемирной организации интеллектуальной собственности (Global Innovation Index), а также рейтинги ESG Country Risk. На одном и том же массиве данных были построены две группы моделей. Первая основана на классической эконометрике панельных данных и включает сквозную регрессию методом наименьших квадратов (МНК), модель с фиксированными эффектами и модель со случайными эффектами. Вторая объединяет четыре алгоритма машинного обучения: Ridge и Lasso как регуляризованные линейные модели, а также Random Forest и Gradient Boosting как ансамблевые методы на основе деревьев решений. Качество моделей сравнивалось на отложенной 20%-ной тестовой выборке по трём метрикам: коэффициенту детерминации (R²), среднеквадратичной ошибке и средней абсолютной ошибке. Полученные результаты свидетельствуют о существенном преимуществе модели Gradient Boosting. Она объяснила 96,8% дисперсии ESG-индекса против 81,2% у обычной линейной регрессии, при этом ошибка прогноза сократилась более чем в два раза — с 5,18 до 2,14 пункта. Данное преимущество связано не только с подбором коэффициентов, но и с различиями в природе рассматриваемых моделей: алгоритмы на основе деревьев решений способны выявлять пороговые эффекты и взаимодействия между переменными, которые в линейной спецификации усредняются в рамках единой функциональной зависимости. Расчёт важности признаков показал, что готовность к использованию искусственного интеллекта и уровень цифровизации совместно формируют более половины объясняющей способности модели, опережая по значимости даже ВВП на душу населения. Отдельный раздел статьи посвящён Узбекистану, индекс цифровизации которого за тринадцать лет увеличился почти втрое. На основе полученных результатов сформулированы три практические рекомендации по совершенствованию национальной системы ESG-мониторинга. EN The study is based on a practical question that public planning authorities in Central Asia are increasingly facing: how reliable are linear models in assessing the impact of digitalization, artificial intelligence, and sustainable development factors, and is their predictive capacity sufficient to describe real socio-economic processes? To address this question, a balanced panel dataset covering 34 developing and transition economies for the period 2012–2024 was constructed, including five Central Asian countries: Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan. The study uses open data from the World Bank (World Development Indicators), the International Telecommunication Union (ICT Development Index), the World Intellectual Property Organization (Global Innovation Index), as well as ESG Country Risk ratings. Two groups of models were developed using the same dataset. The first is based on classical panel-data econometrics and includes pooled ordinary least squares (OLS) regression, a fixed-effects model, and a random-effects model. The second group combines four machine-learning algorithms: Ridge and Lasso as regularized linear models, as well as Random Forest and Gradient Boosting as ensemble methods based on decision trees. Model performance was compared on a 20% holdout test sample using three metrics: the coefficient of determination (R²), root mean squared error, and mean absolute error. The results demonstrate a substantial advantage of the Gradient Boosting model. It explained 96.8% of the variance in the ESG index compared with 81.2% for conventional linear regression, while the prediction error decreased by more than half, from 5.18 to 2.14 points. This advantage is associated not only with coefficient estimation but also with fundamental differences in the nature of the models: decision-tree-based algorithms are capable of identifying threshold effects and interactions among variables that are averaged within a single functional relationship in linear specifications. Feature-importance analysis showed that AI readiness and the level of digitalization jointly account for more than half of the model's explanatory power, exceeding even GDP per capita in importance. A separate section of the article focuses on Uzbekistan, whose digitalization index increased almost threefold over thirteen years. Based on the results obtained, three practical recommendations are formulated for improving the national ESG monitoring system. Ikkinchi guruh toʻrtta mashinaviy oʻrganish algoritmini birlashtiradi: Ridge va Lasso — regulyarlashtirilgan chiziqli modellar sifatida, Random Forest va Gradient Boosting esa qaror daraxtlariga asoslangan ansambl usullari sifatida qoʻllanildi. documents.abstract: Abstract This study presents a bibliometric mapping of the academic literature on airport security, aiming to chart the intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and collaboration patterns of the field and to translate these patterns into implications for security practitioners and policymakers. A total of 1,207 documents indexed in the Scopus database between 2010 and March 2025 were retrieved and analyzed using bibliometric mapping techniques implemented in VOSviewer. Co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, publication-trend, and subject-area analyses were conducted to identify the most influential authors, the dominant research themes, and the disciplinary distribution of the field. The co-authorship network revealed ten major clusters comprising 44 authors and 102 connections, with Adrian Schwaninger emerging as the most central author, reflecting a distinct human-factors research tradition alongside a fast-growing computer-vision tradition. The keyword co-occurrence analysis identified 49 keywords occurring at least six times among 3,062 unique keywords, with “airport security,” “security,” “deep learning,” and “aviation security” as the most frequent terms. Publication output rose markedly after 2019, driven mainly by research on deep learning, X-ray imaging, object detection, and threat-recognition systems. Engineering and computer science were the leading subject areas. Beyond mapping the field, the study translates these findings into concrete implications for airport security operators and regulators, and identifies underexplored themes—including passenger experience, policy design, and the integration of human-factors and automated-detection research—that merit further investigation.

Large language models read text as small pieces called tokens. The number of tokens decides how much text fits in a model’s context window and how much a token-billed service charges. Recent studies show that Indian languages need many more tokens than English, and that Hinglish, which is Hindi written in English letters, creates its own tokenization problems. However, to our knowledge, Marathi, Hindi and several spellings of Hinglish have not been compared side by side as tokenizers have improved. We built 99 parallel sentences in English, Marathi, Hindi and three Hinglish spellings, and counted their tokens with four OpenAI tokenizer encodings, from older to newer. On the oldest encodings, Marathi and Hindi needed 7.4 and 7.6 times as many tokens as English. On the newest, o200k_base, they needed 1.80 and 1.54 times as many. Hinglish needed 1.8 to 2.2 times as many tokens on the oldest encodings and 1.5 to 1.9 times on the newest, so it was much cheaper than Hindi on older tokenizers but not on the newest. Different Hinglish spellings of the same sentence changed token counts by 26% to 31% on average. These results show that the cost of writing in Indian languages depends strongly on the tokenizer and on the script and spelling a user chooses. The data and code are available at https://github.com/samruddhibelsare-max/hinglsh_tokenization_study.

This study examined the comparative effectiveness of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted learning and conventional instructional media among fourth- and fifth-grade elementary school students. Although AI is increasingly promoted as a means of personalizing instruction, empirical evidence directly comparing AI-based and conventional approaches at the elementary level remains limited. A quasi-experimental Pretest-Posttest Control Group Design was employed, involving 42 students in an AI-assisted experimental group and 42 students in a conventionally taught control group drawn from intact classrooms within the same school. Learning effectiveness was operationalized through normalized gain (N-Gain) scores derived from pretest and posttest achievement tests previously established as valid and reliable. Because the experimental group's N-Gain scores departed from a normal distribution, between-group differences were examined using the Mann-Whitney U test, complemented by Cohen's d to estimate practical significance. Results showed that although the two groups began with statistically equivalent pretest scores, the experimental group achieved a significantly higher N-Gain (M = 0.40, medium category) than the control group (M = 0.26, low category), U = 1190.500, p = .006, with a medium effect size (d = 0.551). These findings indicate that AI-assisted learning produced greater and more consistent improvement than conventional media among elementary learners. The study contributes empirical evidence to the underrepresented area of AI-supported elementary education and offers practical guidance for teachers, curriculum developers, and policymakers integrating AI into classroom instruction.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: The contemporary educational landscape is undergoing a radical transition toward data-intensive, interactive paradigms characterized by the integration of sophisticated artificial intelligence and neurosensing technologies. This review examines the convergence of Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) as a transformative force in the creation of "Smart Learning Rooms." By synthesizing current research on Electroencephalography (EEG)-based cognitive monitoring and neural network-driven adaptive systems, this paper delineates a novel conceptual framework for a closed loop pedagogical environment. The study explores the mechanics of real-time attention assessment, the categorization of student learning styles, and the prediction of academic trajectories using diverse ANN architectures, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and multi-layer perceptions. Furthermore, the analysis evaluates the efficacy of neurofeedback in enhancing focus and skill acquisition while addressing the technical, ethical, and socio-economic challenges inherent in the "neuro-digital divide." The proposed framework demonstrates how brain signal monitoring and neural computation can collaborate to personalize instructional pacing, improve engagement, and provide objective performance indicators. The ultimate objective is to provide a rigorous synthesis of the current state of neuro-education and offer a blueprint for the development of fully adaptive, brain-responsive instructional environments.

documents.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with high recurrence rates following curative resection. Accurate non-invasive assessment of tumor aggressiveness and recurrence risk is critical for surgical decision-making and postoperative surveillance, yet remains challenging with conventional imaging modalities. Here, we developed a CT lesion foundation model (LFM), trained via self-supervised learning on 32,120 generic lesion and 6,387 HCC-specific CT patches to capture transferable intra-lesional imaging phenotypes. Across one internal and two external validation cohorts, the sequentially pretrained LFM (LFM-Seq) achieved area under the curve values of 0.916, 0.846, and 0.920 for microvascular invasion (MVI) assessment, and 0.833, 0.885 and 0.795 for pathological grade assessment. The model remained robust under scenarios of limited training data and tumor localization perturbations. Furthermore, LFM-Seq-derived risk scores stratified recurrence-free survival (RFS), yielding an externally validated C-index of 0.701, and remained independently associated with RFS after adjusting for clinicopathological factors. Exploratory biological interpretability analyses showed that LFM-Seq-derived risk phenotypes were associated with suppressed lymphocyte-related immune programs. These results suggest that CT lesion foundation models can support non-invasive and robust characterization of HCC aggressiveness, recurrence risk stratification and discovery of interpretable prognostic imaging biomarkers.

documents.abstract: Musculoskeletal (MSK) modeling is widely used to estimate spinal loading. However, conventional modeling pipelines are computationally intensive and time-consuming, which limit their application for workplace injury risk assessment. This study developed a machine learning (ML) model to predict lumbosacral compression force using intermediate outputs from an MSK modeling workflow. Twenty-one participants completed lifting tasks while marker-based and markerless kinematics were recorded. Reference compression forces were obtained from completed OpenSim simulations, and the resulting dataset was used to train the ML model using three input feature sets. The best-performing model achieved mean root mean square errors of 3.0% with marker-based inputs and 9.9% with markerless inputs. These findings suggest that combining ML with conventional MSK modeling can enable rapid spinal load prediction and may support field deployment when coupled with markerless motion capture. However, given the higher errors observed with markerless input, future work is needed to improve the kinematics accuracy of the markerless system.

Digital transformation in public administration increases the need for personnel information systems that can consolidate fragmented civil-service records and turn them into timely, transparent, and actionable decision support. This study developed SIPINTAR (Integrated, Adaptive, and Responsive Interactive Personnel Intelligence System), an artificial intelligence-based platform designed to integrate civil-service personnel information and support administrative decision-making within an Indonesian government institution. The study adopted a Research and Development approach and implemented the system through a Waterfall-based Software Development Life Cycle. Personnel data from multiple source systems, representing 5,320 civil servants and more than 42,000 historical records for 2019–2025, were integrated using Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) and Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) processes. The integrated data were then subjected to cleaning, transformation, feature engineering, and Random Forest modeling. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, whereas system acceptance was examined through a User Acceptance Test. The strongest reported result was obtained for employee-performance prediction, with 87.24% accuracy, 86% precision, 85% recall, and 85.5% F1-score. Feature-importance analysis as the explainable artificial intelligence component identified performance score, competency level, and years of service as the three most influential variables. The integrated dashboard and AI Assistant provided consolidated access to analytical information, and the UAT result reached 91.40%. Overall, the findings suggest that SIPINTAR can move personnel information management beyond historical record keeping toward predictive and explainable decision support. Nevertheless, the results should be validated with baseline models and broader institutional datasets before being generalized across agencies.

documents.abstract: The purpose of this review is to examine the diagnostic challenges arising from the mathematical biases of the DAS28 index used in monitoring rheumatoid arthritis, as well as the psychological and neurobiological factors underlying patient-physician discordance. Furthermore, this paper aims to analyze the role of digital biomarkers in future decision-making. A structural characteristic of the DAS28 index is that its subjective components carry twice the weight of objective metrics. In cases of central sensitization, depression, or anxiety, this can result in "false-positive" disease activity, leading to unjustified and costly interventions, as well as ineffective therapy. Literature confirms that patient-physician discordance is one of the primary predictors of therapeutic failure, particularly in difficult-to-treat (D2T) cases. The application of the DAS28-P index can help identify pain-dominant phenotypes. Besides musculoskeletal ultrasound, new technologies, such as keystroke dynamics analysis or artificial intelligence-based imaging, offer objective measures to eliminate subjective biases. Modern rheumatological approaches should integrate psychological support, patient education, and pain modulation alongside immunosuppressive treatment. The implementation of digital biomarkers and hybrid care models not only improves the patient's quality of life but also generates significant system-level cost savings in healthcare. Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a new paradigm that allows intelligent systems to behave independently, pursue specific objectives, and adapt to changing circumstances. Agentic AI combines reasoning, planning, memory, learning, and tool utilization to do complicated tasks with minimal human involvement, in contrast to traditional AI systems that mainly react to user inputs. In this article, takes a look at Agentic AI from every angle: its theoretical underpinnings, technological supports, architectural blueprints, and real-world uses. Many models and frameworks are covered, including cognitive and modular designs, systems based on reinforcement learning, hybrid models, and multi-agent systems. Symbolic, probabilistic, and self-reflective reasoning are some of the reasoning methodologies covered. Classical, hierarchical, and adaptive planning strategies are also covered. Agents' ability to reliably and efficiently execute tasks is investigated by looking at memory management, communication protocols, coordination mechanisms, and collaborative decision-making. A wide range of business, medical, financial, academic, and personal aid apps are evaluated in the poll. Privacy, security, computational costs, scalability, and unexpected behavior are the main issues that are highlighted in the end. The study emphasizes the need for more investigation into how to create Agentic AI systems that are reliable, flexible, and effective.

This article compares Abdurauf Fitrat’s principles of terminology formation with contemporary strategies for adapting English artificial intelligence terminology into Uzbek. Its objective is to develop qualitative criteria for evaluating terminological equivalents in relation to meaning, linguistic structure, and communicative use. The material comprises seven selected expressions: artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, neural network, prompt, chatbot, and large language model. Comparative, componential, word formation, and functional pragmatic methods are employed. The analysis distinguishes calquing, direct borrowing, hybrid nomination, and descriptive rendering. It shows that formal similarity to an English source expression does not necessarily guarantee conceptual accuracy or accessibility for readers. The interpretation of prompt depends on context. Fitrat’s linguistic legacy is treated as a historical comparative perspective rather than direct evidence of continuity with digital terminology. A four criterion assessment framework is proposed, covering conceptual precision, structural compatibility, communicative transparency, and terminological consistency. These qualitative conclusions require corpus verification. The framework may inform terminology development.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology capable of enhancing efficiency, decision-making, and resilience in supply chain management. However, its adoption in developing economies remains constrained by several technological, organizational, and environmental challenges. This study examined the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management, with emphasis on the barriers and enablers in developing economies, using Nigeria as the study context. A cross-sectional survey research design was adopted, and data were collected from 235 employees, managers, and supply chain professionals in selected manufacturing firms, logistics companies, retail organizations, and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria using a structured questionnaire titled Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Supply Chain Management Index (AIASCMI). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson Product Moment Correlation. The findings revealed that identified barriers, including inadequate digital infrastructure, high implementation costs, shortage of skilled personnel, and organizational challenges, have a significant negative relationship with the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. The study also found that identified enablers, such as top management support, technological readiness, employee competence, and government support, significantly influence the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence. The study concludes that overcoming existing barriers while strengthening organizational and technological capabilities is essential for the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. It is recommended that organizations invest in digital infrastructure, workforce development, and supportive management practices to maximize the benefits of Artificial Intelligence and improve supply chain performance.

documents.abstract: Background and Purpose: The rapid transition from deterministic automation and passive algorithmic decision-support systems to agentic artificial intelligence (Agentic AI) represents an unprecedented ontological shift in enterprise information systems (IS). Unlike antecedent generative models that merely synthesize conversational text, agentic AI operates with persistent internal memory, autonomous multi-step cognitive reasoning, goal decomposition, and self-directed tool and API execution. In contemporary digital organizations, these autonomous systems are progressively onboarded, provisioned, and treated not merely as passive software artifacts, but as synthetic workers or "digital employees." However, this conceptual elevation fractures foundational organizational assumptions rooted in classical agency theory, sociotechnical systems theory, and managerial control architectures. This monograph investigates how enterprise deployment of digital employees redefines the boundaries of delegation, moral and organizational accountability, and managerial control within IS-enabled organizational environments. Design, Methodology, and Approach: To rigorously interrogate this emergent socio-algorithmic reality, an extensive explanatory mixed-methods research design was executed across a 24-month longitudinal investigation (2024-2026). The quantitative phase collected and analyzed empirical survey data from 482 senior enterprise leaders, Chief Information Officers (CIOs), Chief AI Officers (CAIOs), Enterprise Architects, and line managers across four knowledge-intensive industry verticals (Financial Services & FinTech, Healthcare & HealthTech, Global Supply Chain Logistics, and Enterprise Cloud/SaaS). Structural Equation Modeling using Partial Least Squares (PLS-SEM) was employed to empirically test the structural dependencies between perceived agentic autonomy, algorithmic trust, delegation depth, operational agility, and accountability drift. The qualitative phase comprised 38 semi-structured, in-depth key-informant interviews and four comprehensive, longitudinal multi-case studies examining end-to-end organizational deployments of multi-agent architectures (including LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, and proprietary enterprise agent meshes). Rigorous thematic analysis and qualitative comparative synthesis were conducted to deconstruct operational failures, behavioral drift phenomena, and governance adaptations. Empirical Findings: The empirical results reveal a profound structural paradox in enterprise agentic delegation. First, the transition from "task offloading" to "autonomous mandate delegation" generates a statistically significant positive effect on organizational agility (β=0.495, p<0.001) and operational velocity, but concurrently fuels a critical "accountability void" and organizational drift (β=0.342, p<0.001). Second, traditional managerial control frameworks specifically diagnostic and boundary controls suffer severe operational degradation when confronted with non-deterministic agentic planning and recursive API invocation. Third, human supervisors frequently exhibit either "cognitive abandonment" (over-trusting autonomous agents due to perceived competence) or severe "algorithmic cynicism" (resorting to micro-surveillance that negates agentic throughput benefits). Fourth, the investigation reveals the emergence of what we conceptualize as the "Synthetic Moral Crumple Zone," wherein middle-tier human managers are held legally and administratively accountable for unforeseen agentic systemic errors that they possessed neither the technical visibility nor the temporal window to prevent.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in English language education is reshaping traditional pedagogical frameworks, fostering learner autonomy, and redefining the educator’s role. This article presents a conceptual framework and pedagogical model exploring how AI-driven portfolio assessment and custom AI language models can be integrated within an Agile learning framework to support iterative, self-directed learning. While AI enhances language acquisition through personalized feedback and adaptive learning, concerns about authenticity, plagiarism, and over-reliance on AI-generated content remain. A structured approach to AI literacy development is introduced, ensuring that students critically assess AI-generated feedback rather than passively accepting it. A key component of this framework is AI-supported reflection, where learners evaluate AI suggestions based on alignment with their authentic voice and intended meaning. This process is reinforced through an AI-reflection rubric designed to cultivate metacognitive awareness and critical engagement with AI outputs. Agile methodologies, particularly iterative learning cycles, scaffold AI-supported writing assignments, balancing human and AI feedback for progressive skill development. The article also examines configurable AI tools for assessment, such as custom GPTs within ChatGPT and Gems within Google Gemini, which can evaluate language proficiency, track learning progression, and facilitate AI-supported peer assessment. The framework is designed to be adaptable across international EFL and ESL contexts, supporting authentic learning rather than replacing the learner’s central role in the learning process.

Online businesses must answer product questions, explain policies, guide purchases and resolve order-related concerns across multiplechannels. Human-only support can be costly and slow during peak demand, while rigid rule-based chatbots struggle with varied wording andmulti-step questions. This paper presents a conceptual design for an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chat Assistant for Online Business thatcombines natural language understanding, retrieval from approved business knowledge, controlled access to commerce services andescalation to human staff. The proposed assistant interprets customer intent, retrieves relevant product and policy information, generatesgrounded responses, and invokes permitted actions such as checking order status only after appropriate authentication. The architectureemphasizes factual consistency, privacy, security, accessibility and measurable service quality. It also describes a developmentmethodology, evaluation metrics, risk controls and a staged deployment plan. Since this is a design-oriented study, no original performanceresults are claimed; the proposed evaluation must be conducted using representative customer queries and verified business data.

Conventional drug discovery and development is associated with substantial financial costs, lengthy development timelines, and high attrition rates during preclinical and clinical evaluation. Drug repurposing provides an alternative strategy by identifying new therapeutic applications for existing drugs with previously characterized pharmacological and safety profiles. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, multimodal biomedical data integration, mechanistic modelling, and digital twin technology have created new opportunities to improve computational drug repurposing and patient-specific treatment prediction. This review examines the emerging integration of AI-driven digital twins with drug repurposing, focusing on digital twin architectures, artificial intelligence methodologies multi modal data integration, drug target prediction, pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic modelling, treatment-response simulation, and personalized therapeutic decision-making. The review also discusses applications across cancer, neurodegenerative, cardiovascular, infectious, metabolic, and rare diseases. Particular emphasis is placed on the development of patient-specific digital twins, integration of multi-omics and clinical data, virtual treatment simulation, and validation through computational, experimental, and clinical approaches. Major challenges include data heterogeneity, interoperability, model reliability, uncertainty quantification, interpretability, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity, privacy, clinical workflow integration, and regulatory acceptance. Emerging approaches, including causal AI, federated learning, multimodal foundation models, virtual clinical trials, and real-time adaptive digital twins, may further enhance the translational potential of AI-enabled drug repurposing. However, prospective clinical validation and standardized regulatory frameworks remain necessary before widespread clinical implementation.

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence currently determines how individuals access information, services and decisions from institutions. The influence of this technology raises questions about how the law can hold those who control such power accountable under the constitution. In this article I investigate if the developing governance framework in India protects digital rights and offers ways to fix harm caused by artificial intelligence. It applies to a qualitative doctrinal method to examine constitutional guarantees, court decisions, laws plus official policies. To assist this analysis, the text includes a comparison of two international instruments. The discussion distinguishes between constitutional duties, laws that the state has passed but not fully started, secondary regulations and governance principles that lack binding force. I argue that protecting privacy does not solve the problems of unfair classification, hidden decision processes, or deception. Privacy laws do not address how companies spread responsibility across long supply chains. India uses a strategy that focuses on innovation and treats different industries separately - this method is flexible, but it is only legitimate if the state provides rules for fair procedures but also ways for citizens to complain. In response, I propose a framework for constitutional accountability - this framework connects the requirement for a legal basis, the balance of interests, equal treatment and clear explanations. It also requires that a human reviews decisions and that victims receive a fix for their injuries. The specific recommendations include tests to see how important uses of technology affect society. There must be records that allow independent experts to check the system. On top of this the state must use safeguards when it buys technology. Responsibility is assigned to the party who controls risks that they can predict.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: WP_AI_8.5 develops a three-object framework for clarifying what AI governance is actually governing. The paper begins from a structural problem in contemporary AI governance. Technical systems, human decision-makers, institutional actors, oversight mechanisms, accountability, safety, and responsibility are often discussed within the same governance language without clearly separating the objects to which those rules apply. This can produce governance object drift, in which the focus of governance shifts during analysis, and governance subject inversion, in which AI becomes increasingly personalized as the apparent actor while the humans and institutions exercising real authority become less visible. The paper identifies three distinct but connected objects of AI governance. The first is the AI entity itself. The paper distinguishes four governance identities: Tool, System, Agent, and Autonomous Actor. These categories are not claims about consciousness or legal personhood. They describe different operational relationships between AI capability, delegated authority, persistence, external consequence, and human reauthorization. The second object is the human authority structure across the AI lifecycle. Developers, testers, providers, approvers, regulators, administrators, operators, and users exercise different forms of authority and therefore require different forms of governance. Human conduct must remain a direct object of AI governance rather than being displaced by anthropomorphic descriptions of AI behavior. The third object is the institutional interface through which AI capability enters society. Admission, authorization, release, deployment, access, supervision, review, restriction, suspension, and withdrawal determine how technical capability becomes socially operative. The paper also distinguishes Governance Identity Drift from Governance Object Drift. The former occurs when an AI system’s actual operational identity changes while its formal governance category remains unchanged. The latter occurs when governance itself shifts its analytical object, for example when a human authorization decision is gradually redescribed as autonomous machine behavior. The central argument is that governance must define its own objects rather than inherit them passively from technical narratives. AI should be governed according to what kind of operational entity it is. Humans and institutions should be governed according to the authority they exercise. The human-AI institutional interface should be governed according to the social consequences it enables. WP_AI_8.5 builds on the preceding papers in the WP_AI_8 series. WP_AI_8.1 established the engineering circuit-breaker principle; WP_AI_8.2 examined responsibility escape; WP_AI_8.3 developed a dual-track framework connecting capability control and human responsibility; and WP_AI_8.4 addressed the conditions under which AI capability may move from controlled development into social release. WP_AI_8.5 moves one level upward by clarifying the governance objects to which those mechanisms apply.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Abstract The accelerating adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in human resource management (HRM) raises important questions about which AI-driven interventions most effectively enhance workforce agility, decision-making, and employee outcomes. This study investigated the effects of multiple AI applications—including employee wellbeing (AIEEW), performance management (AIPM), recruitment and selection (AIRS), training and development (AITD), and strategic HR practices (AISHRP), on HR process efficiency (HRPE), decision-making agility (DMA), workplace AI integration (WAI), and enhanced HRM effectiveness (EHRE). Data was collected from 256 professionals in organizational and educational institutions and analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) with SmartPLS. Results revealed that eight of nine hypothesized paths were supported, with AI-enabled wellbeing exerting the strongest effect on workplace AI integration (β = 0.583, p < .001). Recruitment and performance management systems significantly enhanced HR process efficiency, while strategic HR planning and talent analytics improved decision-making agility. HR performance enhancement strongly predicted HR effectiveness (β = 0.458, p < .001), highlighting process efficiency as a key mediator of AI’s impact. Two paths were weaker: AI in training and development did not significantly affect HR process efficiency, and decision-making agility showed only marginal influence on HRM effectiveness. Theoretically, the study enriches the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory by demonstrating how AI functions as both a strategic resource and a capability-building tool. Practically, findings suggest that organizations should prioritize wellbeing, recruitment, and HR performance systems when investing in AI, while ensuring that training platforms and decision-support tools are better integrated into HR processes.

documents.abstract: Despite growing emphasis on inclusive education, mathematics classrooms still exhibit disparities arising from cognitive, linguistic, socioeconomic, and systemic barriers, marginalizing diverse students and limiting equitable learning opportunities. Artificial intelligence (AI) presents considerable potential for addressing these challenges. This study investigates how AI technologies can be harnessed to create mathematics classrooms that are inclusive and adaptive to individual student needs. Anchored in Universal Design for Learning (UDL) and the Substitution, Augmentation, Modification, Redefinition (SAMR) frameworks, the study explores how AI functionalities can facilitate personalized learning, responsive instruction, and equitable participation. The study employs a hybrid conceptual–structured narrative review approach, synthesizing existing literature through structured searching, screening, thematic coding, and conceptual integration. The synthesis examines AI functionalities, inclusive pedagogical affordances, implementation challenges, ethical and equity concerns, and future directions. On this basis, the study develops the Synergistic AI-Inclusive Mathematics Education (SAIME) framework, conceptualizing UDL as an inclusion-oriented design foundation, SAMR as a technological transformation pathway, and teacher-mediated pedagogy and ethical safeguards as essential conditions for equitable outcomes in access, participation, and achievement. It concludes that AI can contribute meaningfully to inclusive mathematics education when its technological affordances are purposefully aligned with inclusive pedagogy, ethical and equity safeguards, and equitable learning goals.

UV–Visible (UV–Vis) spectrophotometry is a rapid, economical and widely available technique for pharmaceutical analysis, but its selectivity is limited when the drugs in a formulation have overlapping absorption spectra. The integration of chemometrics and artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning (ML) algorithms such as partial least squares (PLS), principal component regression (PCR), support vector regression (SVR), artificial neural networks (ANN) and random forests, with intelligent wavelength selection and metaheuristic optimization (genetic and Firefly algorithms), allows the simultaneous quantification of several active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) from the whole spectrum rather than a single wavelength. This review summarizes the principles of UV–Vis spectroscopy, the current status of AI-assisted UV–Vis analysis, and the challenges related to model interpretability, data integrity, validation and instrument variability. Applications, drawbacks and futureprospects are discussed, including process analytical technology (PAT), portable instruments, green analytical chemistry and regulatory acceptance of AI-enabled spectroscopic methods as complementary tools to chromatographic assays in pharmaceutical quality control.

documents.abstract: Software development often requires programmers to write repetitive code, understand unfamiliar requirements, and spend considerabletime identifying and correcting errors. Recent advances in artificial intelligence have enabled systems to generate source code fromnatural-language instructions. However, generated code may contain syntax errors, incorrect logic, insecure patterns, or incompletehandling of edge cases. This paper proposes an AI-Based Code Generation and Self-Testing System that accepts a programming task innatural language, generates a candidate solution, prepares or selects test cases, executes the code in a controlled environment, and analysesthe results. The proposed workflow combines prompt interpretation, code generation, static validation, test-case generation, sandboxedexecution, and feedback-based refinement. The system is intended to support developers and learners by reducing repetitive effort andproviding an initial validation cycle. It does not replace code review or guarantee correctness; execution safety, test coverage, modellimitations, and human verification remain important. This paper presents a proposed methodology and evaluation plan. Quantitativeperformance claims should be added only after implementation and testing.

Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered customer service systems have expanded across Saudi Arabia’s retail sector during 2025–2026, with major retailers increasingly exploring chatbots, recommendation engines, and automated service technologies. Official Saudi digital-economy statistics document the wider shift towards digital commerce, although online-shopping participation should not be interpreted as a direct measure of AI adoption or retailer-specific investment. This study examines the relationship among AI service quality, emotional brand attachment, and brand loyalty using survey results reported for 512 retail customers in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, collected between May and September 2026. Using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and bootstrap resampling, the analysis reports a positive direct association between AI service quality and loyalty (β = 0.421, p < 0.001), together with a positive indirect association through emotional brand attachment (reported indirect effect = 0.238, 95% CI [0.187, 0.289]). The study considers a possible “mechanical efficiency paradox”: functional improvements in AI service may be more strongly associated with loyalty than with emotional attachment. Importantly, this survey does not include a direct comparison with human-delivered service, and the reported positive attachment coefficient (β = 0.187) cannot establish that AI decreases attachment. The reported gender subgroup estimates differ: the AI quality–attachment association is positive for male respondents (β = 0.289, p = 0.001) and statistically nonsignificant for female respondents (β = −0.023, p = 0.811). Age-specific estimates also vary, with more positive reported coefficients in younger groups, although the statistical significance of the age differences requires further supporting output. The manuscript reports that the model accounts for 51.2% of the variance in loyalty (R2 = 0.512) and has positive predictive relevance (Q2 = 0.289). Because some path estimates, correlations, and variance-explained values are not mutually consistent, these results require rechecking against the original SmartPLS output before publication. Managerial implications include offering hybrid AI–human service, allowing customers to choose their preferred channel, and maintaining personal attention for complex or emotionally sensitive interactions. The findings provide a framework for assessing how technological service quality and relationship-building might jointly contribute to brand loyalty.
topics: Consumer Behavior in Brand Consumption and Identification

documents.abstract: Pharmaceutical marketing is being reshaped by the growing use of digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) in communication, customer engagement, and commercial decision-making. Promotion that once relied almost entirely on medical representatives, face-to-face physician visits, product detailing, and printed material is now supplemented, and in some cases reshaped, by digital platforms, social media, e-detailing, webinars, data analytics, and omnichannel communication. This review looks at how AI is being applied to pharmaceutical digital marketing, with particular attention to machine learning, predictive analytics, segmentation of customers and healthcare professionals, personalized communication, customer relationship management, generative AI, and omnichannel engagement. Evidence from the published literature suggests that digital channels widen the reach and flexibility of pharmaceutical communication, while AI adds the ability to analyse large datasets, anticipate behaviour, segment audiences, and personalize content at scale. At the same time, this shift brings its own set of problems: data privacy, inconsistent data quality, algorithmic bias, the risk of misinformation, limited transparency, regulatory compliance, and the continued need for human oversight all surface repeatedly in the literature. Empirical studies also indicate that digital engagement can shape how healthcare professionals are communicated with, influence prescribing-related behaviour, and affect consumer attitudes, though the size of this effect depends heavily on the channel, audience, and therapeutic area involved. Taken together, the evidence points toward a future in which human expertise, digital communication, and AI-supported decision-making work alongside one another rather than one replacing the other. For this model to be sustainable, pharmaceutical marketing will need to be built on responsible implementation, ethical communication, evidence-based content, and clear governance.

Practical writing is an important component of senior high school English teaching. he English Curriculum Standards for Senior High School (2017 edition, 2020 revision) requires students to select appropriate language forms according to the identity of the communicative partner, he occasion and the degree of formality, o as to achieve effective cross-cultural communication. owever, urrent practical writing teaching in Grade 10 still suffers from mechanical format training, eak reader awareness, nappropriate register control, nd single and delayed feedback. Although generative artificial intelligence offers new possibilities for writing instruction, existing studies have focused mainly on automated essay scoring, academic writing at the tertiary level, or continuation writing tasks, and few have systematically constructed an AI-empowered mechanism and teaching pathway for senior high school practical writing from the perspective of the integration of teaching, learning and assessment. Adopting a conceptual construction and lesson design orientation, and grounded in the cognitive process theory of writing,t he technology-enhanced language learning framework, self-efficacy theory and formative assessment theory, this study proposes a “5A+E” empowerment mechanism model, comprising Analysis, Activation, Assistance, Assessment, Adaptation, and Ethics. On this basis, a five-stage teaching pathway—context trigger, element deconstruction, AI co-writing, multi-dimensional evaluation, and reflective transfer—is designed, and a lesson on the invitation letter for the “Chinese Culture Festival” is presented. The study argues that AI can serve as a reader analyst, format validator, point generator, register regulator and evaluation embedder, moving practical writing instruction from template drilling toward authentic communication. As a theoretical construction and lesson design study, this paper has not yet been empirically tested; future action research or quasi-experimental studies are needed to validate and refine the model and pathway.

Grievance redressal is where citizens test whether government listens. Indian governments receive millions of complaints each year through portals, call centres, social media, letters and in-person visits. The volume, the variety of languages and the number of departments involved make it hard to route complaints correctly, resolve them on time and learn from patterns. Artificial intelligence (AI), and in particular natural language processing for Indian languages, can help with each of these steps — but only if it is introduced with clear safeguards and with officers, not algorithms, remaining accountable for decisions. This paper proposes a five-layer framework for AI-enabled grievance redressal in Indian states: (1) multilingual, multichannel intake; (2) classification, routing and prioritisation; (3) officer assistance for resolution; (4) closure verification and citizen feedback; and (5) analytics for root-cause and policy learning. For each layer it sets out what AI can do, the human checks required and suitable performance measures. It also discusses governance, data protection and change-management requirements, and suggests a phased path from pilot to state-wide adoption. The paper is a design framework drawn from e-governance practice and the published literature; it does not report results from a deployed system.

The continued growth of mobile data traffic is placing increasing demands on radio access networks (RANs).Although 4G and 5G networks already use sophisticated automation to manage radio resources, conventionaloptimisation methods can struggle to respond efficiently to rapidly changing traffic patterns, complex interferenceconditions and variations in user behaviour. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer an opportunityto make network management more predictive by identifying patterns in network data, forecasting demand andsupporting more adaptive resource allocation. This article examines the development of AI-native RAN, focusing onthe UK 5G environment. It reviews radio resource management, predictive optimisation and emerging AI-RANarchitectures, including the O-RAN Intelligent Controller framework. It considers the O2–Nokia live deploymentannounced at London Paddington in October 2026 and BT's planned AI-RAN trial with Nokia and NVIDIA inBirmingham during 2027. It also examines data quality, model reliability, security, interoperability, computingoverhead and human oversight. The article argues that AI-native RAN should be treated as an evolution ofestablished radio engineering, with benefits demonstrated through measurable improvements in network efficiency,reliability and customer experience.

This paper provides a comprehensive critical analysis of algorithmic bias in human resource management, examining how artificial intelligence (AI) systems used in hiring, promotions, and performance management can perpetuate and amplify societal biases. Moving beyond conventional discussions of bias, this research introduces a series of novel theoretical frameworks to uncover the deeper, systemic mechanisms through which algorithmic HR systems produce inequitable outcomes. These include the Sociotechnical Bias Amplification Model (SBAM), which explains how temporal bias, intersectional bias, and feedback loops interact to compound discrimination; the Algorithmic Opacity Paradox, which argues that the perceived objectivity of AI obscures its discriminatory potential; and the Fairness Impossibility Theorem in the HR context, which demonstrates the mathematical and normative trade-offs inherent in any algorithmic fairness definition. The paper further develops a critical perspective by introducing concepts such as data colonialism, the performance management panopticon, and the algorithmic accountability gap. Through a synthesis of technical literature, organizational theory, and critical algorithm studies, this research argues that the challenge of algorithmic bias is not merely a technical problem of “debiasing” but a fundamental crisis of legitimacy for automated decision-making in the workplace. The analysis is supported by clearly labelled conceptual diagrams and selected empirical findings drawn from published research. It concludes with a set of actionable recommendations for HR leaders, policymakers, and researchers, advocating for a shift from a technical-fix mindset to a more holistic, human-centered approach to governance that prioritizes justice, accountability, and equity.

documents.abstract: This review assesses ecological engineering solutions for landslide prevention and slope stabilization by synthesizing evidence identified through scientific databases. The review encompasses the idea of applying vegetation-based techniques, including live stakes, brush layering, revegetation, grasses, herbaceous plants, bamboo plantations, and lithophytic life forms, together with conventional and structural measures such as natural geotextiles, live wooden crib walls, wattle fences, live silt fences, and live gully breaks. The reviewed evidence highlights the importance of species with strong root systems, which can influence the effectiveness of bioengineering interventions. Species such as Vetiver, Bermuda Grass, Ryegrass, Alder, selected Ficus species, and bamboo show deep-rooted control over soil reinforcement, erosion, and slope stabilization, while lithophytic life forms and pioneer colonizers may support the restoration of exposed rocky and landslide-affected surfaces. The review also examines the contribution of artificial intelligence, remote sensing, unmanned aerial vehicles, LiDAR, interferometric synthetic aperture radar, and machine learning models in landslide susceptibility assessment, monitoring, and advance warning. Overall, the findings revealed that integrated ecological engineering and data-driven monitoring may complement conventional stabilization measures, reduce landslide risk, restore degraded slopes, and inform sustainable land-management planning.

This research is motivated by the high turnover of contract employees in the Operational Division of PT. XYZ which has an impact on increasing recruitment needs, disrupting company operations, and decreasing productivity. The study aims to analyze employee retention factors including organizational components, career opportunities, rewards, job design, and employee relations. The method used is a qualitative approach supported by descriptive analysis using the Weight Mean Score (WMS). Data were collected through observation, questionnaires to 61 contract employees, semi-structured interviews with five informants, and documentation. Data analysis was carried out through data reduction, data presentation, drawing conclusions, and WMS analysis. The results of the study indicate that all factors are in the good category, namely organizational components (3.66), career opportunities (3.58), rewards (3.68), job design (3.62), and employee relations (3.52). However, the company still needs to improve work facilities, transparency of promotions and career paths, fairness of rewards, job variety, and communication between superiors and employees. The study concludes that these five factors contribute to supporting contract employee retention at PT. XYZ.
